# Ordinance No. 04, Series of 2001

**Ordinance imposing fees for slaughtered animals in Pitogo, Quezon**

## Summary

This ordinance regulates and imposes fees for the slaughter of animals within the municipality of Pitogo, Quezon. It aims to ensure proper sanitation and generate revenue for the municipality. The ordinance specifies the fees to be collected for each type of animal slaughtered and outlines penalties for violations.

## Key Provisions

1.  **Section 1.** Imposes fees for animals slaughtered within the municipality, the revenue from which will be used for sanitation and other related expenses.
2.  **Section 2.** Specifies that the fees collected will be used for the expenses related to sanitation and other related expenses.
3.  **Section 3.** States that the ordinance covers all areas within the municipality of Pitogo.
4.  **Section 4.** Defines the amount to be paid for each type of animal slaughtered.
5.  **Section 5.** Instructs the Barangay Agricultural Officer and the Chief of Police to implement the ordinance.
6.  **Section 6.** States that anyone caught slaughtering animals without paying the required fee will be fined One Thousand Pesos (₱1,000.00) or imprisoned for five (5) days to a maximum of nine (9) days, or both, at the discretion of the court. All fines collected will be used for the municipality's projects, as determined by the Municipal Mayor or the Opinion of the Inspekt-Heneral.
7.  **Section 7.** States that any ordinance that contradicts this ordinance will be subject to a fifty percent (50%) penalty on the value of the fine.
8.  **Section 8.** States that any part of this ordinance that is found to be invalid will not affect the validity of the remaining provisions.
9.  **Section 9.** Requires the posting of the ordinance in the bulletin board of the [[Sangguniang Bayan]] and in conspicuous places within the municipality for ten (10) consecutive days.
10. **Section 10.** The ordinance shall take effect upon its approval by the [[Sangguniang Bayan]] of Pitogo, Quezon on October 29, [[2001]].
